hook_text: A sailor stops a drifting boat in two seconds with no knot at all. Meet the cleat.
clip_script: A cleat is a rope holder. Horn cleat: one turn round the base, two figure-of-eights over the horns, and friction at every bend takes the load. Lift the turns off and the rope runs free. Cam cleat: two toothed jaws on springs; pull the rope down and they grip, pull back and they bite harder, a ratchet for rope. Jam cleat: a tapered slot; pull to the narrow end and it wedges. All three: the harder the rope pulls, the harder it holds. None adds force; they only decide whether the rope moves. Bolt them through, size them to the rope, and check them wet.
visual_style: Whiteboard horn cleat with figure-of-eight turns appearing; cam jaws pinching a rope; a tapered slot with a rope wedging; a flagpole and a pontoon in quick cuts.
pacing: Two-second mooring, wrap, pinch, jam, the harder the better, no force added, fix it right.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the cleat on your school flagpole.
